business_ops.supply_chain_integration: BACKWARD INTEGRATION — the issuer describes itself as a vertically integrated 'microbe-to-pharmacy' and 'farm-to-pharmacy' platform: commodity plant-based derivative inputs (soy-derived sterols/phytosterols) are biotransformed in-house into corticosteroid and hormone precursors, then converted through multi-step chemical synthesis (up to 400 cGMP-validated synthesis steps) into finished APIs, "with in-house control over each step, from raw material to final API production". The stated commercial effect: "This integration allows us to make strategic, cost-effective 'make versus buy' decisions for key starting materials ('KSMs') for over 80% of our products by revenue, thereby reducing external dependence for sourcing intermediates from other geographies" (a parallel sentence puts the same 80%+ against "our product portfolio by revenue"). The issuer claims to be "among the few backward-integrated Indian and global manufacturers capable of producing in-house corticosteroid and hormone precursors, as of June 30, 2025" — ATTRIBUTED TO THE COMMISSIONED F&S REPORT. Fermentation spans four modalities: biotransformation of soy-derived sterols; classical fermentation for pipeline APIs; recombinant protein expression (GLP-1, Insulins); and precision fermentation / synthetic biology for nutraceuticals and alternate proteins. Multi-scale fermenters (5 KL, 35 KL, 100 KL) allow both low-volume/high-value and high-volume products. FORWARD INTEGRATION — into complex injectables: "We are one of the first generics companies globally to successfully develop DCV through backward integration, by relying on in-house materials and not imports, for Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate injection and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate" (Source: F&S Report), extending the chain from API to finished double-chamber vials, bags and syringes at the Mhow Facility. RESIDUAL EXTERNAL DEPENDENCE — imports remain material and China-concentrated: raw material imports were 13.79% / 19.67% / 55.43% / 37.79% of total expenses in Q1FY26 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23, of which China alone accounted for 11.76% / 16.82% / 52.79% / 34.00%; raw materials are procured on purchase orders rather than long-term contracts, and the top ten suppliers were 17.90% / 18.41% / 50.33% / 34.95% of total expenses. Downstream logistics are outsourced: "We transport our products via road, sea, and air ... We engage third-party logistics service providers to facilitate our transportation needs." Procurement and inventory run on a "qualified vendor base integrated with SAP-driven material management to ensure traceability and inventory control", with SCADA and Distributed Control System for real-time process control. Sustainability: renewable energy (solar and wind), carbon-neutral bio-briquettes, zero liquid discharge and re-use of treated water across all sites; continuous flow chemistry implemented for Progesterone.

Product-level volume market shares in Fiscal 2025: Hydrocortisone 78.9%, Testosterone 70.4%, Methylprednisolone 50.6%. Positioning is niche: revenue is almost entirely from APIs (100.00%, 99.10%, 100.00% and 100.00% of revenue from operations in the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023) concentrated in a specialised corticosteroid / steroidal-hormone and fermentation API franchise rather than a broad-based pharmaceutical portfolio. opportunities: Expand the product portfolio across steroidal-hormones and classical fermentation-based APIs (Mupirocin, Teicoplanin and Serratiopeptidase already launched; planned additions include Vegan Vitamin D3 and algal-based Docosa Hexanoic Acid, and steroidal derivatives such as vitamin D2 and D3 using photochemistry)

Commercialise a generic alternative to Premarin (conjugated estrogens): Premarin, sold by Pfizer, generated global sales of USD 380 million in 2024 and has only one generic substitute (Source: F&S Report); the Company is among the few globally to have developed a complex API with 82 US FDA mandated components

Build on fermentation capabilities and expand biotechnology offerings such as GLP-1 analogues and Insulin, manufactured at the Pithampur Facility with validation and customer agreements in place, plus a dedicated 14 KL biologics fermentation unit (two reactors of 7 KL each) planned at Ujjain

Scale up diverse CDMO offerings based on three interlinked differentiated platform technologies, including food/nutraceutical, alternative protein, enzyme and industrial biotechnology work at the newly commissioned Ujjain Facility (maximum capacity 400 KL)
Commercialise complex injectables through differentiated drug-device combinations built on the double-chamber vial platform
Continue to invest in new technologies and R&D for product optimisation, including automation, digitalisation and AI-driven process optimisation across laboratories and manufacturing facilities
Partner with large pharmaceutical companies for difficult-to-execute projects, structured as risk- and reward-sharing collaborations beyond standard CDMO services

China+1 sourcing shift: gradual movement of fermentation API production away from China amid geopolitical concerns, supply chain vulnerabilities and stricter environmental norms, with an observed rise in requests for proposals from global pharmaceutical companies (Source: F&S Report)

Rising global prevalence of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases driving corticosteroid demand, and expanding hormone API demand from reproductive health, metabolic disorder and hormone replacement therapies
strengths: Global leadership in corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs in volume and value terms as of Fiscal 2025, with global volume market share of 36.2% in corticosteroid and 44.2% in steroidal-hormone APIs (Source: F&S Report)

Only Indian and global company present across the top 10 corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs in Fiscal 2025; over 60 corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs in sterile and non-sterile formats, covering 90% of the market (Source: F&S Report)

Highest revenue among Indian API manufacturers from sale of corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs in the three preceding Fiscals as of June 30, 2025, having backward integrated into in-house corticosteroid and hormone precursors

Regulatory credentials as of June 30, 2025: 42 DMFs registered with the US FDA and 23 CEPs from the EDQM; Rau and Pithampur facilities accredited by US FDA, WHO-GMP, EU-GMP and others; 10 regulatory-agency inspections and over 106 customer audits completed over the last three Fiscals and the three months period ended June 30, 2025

Vertically integrated farm/microbe-to-pharmacy platform with maximum fermentation capacity of 700 KL, supporting cost-effective make-versus-buy decisions for KSMs covering over 80% of the product portfolio by revenue

Fully-invested manufacturing base: total capacity of 584.67 MT aggregate maximum chemical synthesis, 700 KL fermentation and 20 million vials for complex injectables; over Rs 7,405.16 million invested in API and injectables capacity over the last three Fiscals and the three months period ended June 30, 2025

Long-standing customer base: over 200 customers in more than 40 countries as of June 30, 2025 (more than 50 domestic and 150 export customers); average relationship tenure of more than ten years for the top five and more than nine years for the top ten customers; 35 new customers added in the three months ended June 30, 2025 and 96, 89 and 68 in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023

Differentiated chemistry enabling APIs and products with up to 400 synthesis steps validated under cGMP; three dedicated R&D centres in Indore covering organic chemistry, biotechnology and complex injectables (over 50 organic-chemistry scientists and 15 complex-injectables scientists as of June 30, 2025)

Backward-integrated double-chamber vial (DCV) technology for Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate injections, a combined US market of USD 204 million; among the first generics companies globally to achieve this via backward integration (Source: F&S Report)

Per the F&S Report operating benchmark of Indian peers, Symbiotec is the only benchmarked peer shown with double-chamber / drug-device combination capability, and among the few with complex lyophilization, precision fermentation and synthetic biology; it outranked benchmarked Indian peers on EBITDA CAGR and PAT CAGR and ranked second on operating revenue CAGR between Fiscal 2023 and Fiscal 2025
threats: Highly competitive market, with competition within API manufacturing and against full-service pharmaceutical outsourcing / CDMO companies; competitors may possess greater technical, manufacturing, R&D, sales, marketing and financial resources, may accept lower returns to increase market share, and may commercialise similar products first

Regulatory action risk: manufacturing facilities are subject to periodic inspections and audits by regulatory authorities and customers, and manufacturing or quality-control failures could trigger regulatory action; injectables face significantly more stringent oversight than oral generics on sterility assurance, endotoxin and particulate control and aseptic processing, and many injectable generics require bioequivalence studies

Export exposure: revenue from external customers outside India was 66.67%, 55.19%, 59.97% and 52.76% of revenue from operations in the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023

internal_operational.detail: Revenue from external customers outside India (Ind AS 108) represented 66.67%, 55.19%, 59.97% and 52.76% of revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. As of June 30, 2025 the company supplied over 200 customers in over 40 countries and held 42 DMFs registered with the US FDA and 23 CEPs from the EDQM. Listed export risks include changes in foreign laws and trade policy, pricing pressure per jurisdiction, sanctions, FX movement, regulatory inspections and complex tax regimes; the DRHP states there was no non-compliance in overseas markets resulting in penalties in the last three Fiscals and Q1 FY2026.
internal_operational.title: Export concentration: 66.67% of revenue from external customers outside India in Q1 FY2026

internal_operational.detail: Revenue from the United States represented 11.61%, 4.02%, 8.97% and 4.39% of revenue from operations in Q1 FY2026 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. In August 2025 the United States implemented 50% tariffs on imports of goods in various sectors from India, excluding the pharmaceutical sector. On September 25, 2025 the United States announced that effective October 1, 2025, 100% tariffs would be imposed on all branded / patented pharmaceutical products manufactured outside the United States, unless the manufacturer is building a plant in the United States. The DRHP states no tariffs have yet been imposed on pharmaceutical goods other than branded / patented products imported from India and that results of operations have not been directly impacted; the company states it cannot quantify the expected impact.
internal_operational.evidence: US revenue: 11.61% (3M FY26), 4.02% (FY25), 8.97% (FY24), 4.39% (FY23) of revenue from operations. August 2025: 50% US tariffs on Indian goods in various sectors (pharma excluded). September 25, 2025 announcement, effective October 1, 2025: 100% tariffs on branded / patented pharmaceutical products manufactured outside the US.
internal_operational.title: US tariff exposure: 11.61% of Q1 FY2026 revenue from the United States

concerns_observed: Half the capital base is not yet earning. As of June 30, 2025, 53.32% of the Gross Block of ₹13,195.00 million and 53.29% of capital employed of ₹7,405.16 million are stated as yet to be fully commercialised. The complex-injectables facility at Mhow, established with an investment of ₹3,370.34 million and capable of 20 million double chamber vials a year, prints '-' for 'Sale of complex injectables' in Q1FY26, FY25, FY24 and FY23 alike; CDMO earned ₹68.00 million (0.90% of revenue from operations) in FY25 and nil in Q1FY26; APIs were 99.10% to 100.00% of revenue from operations in every period presented.

The Company's own headline return ratio only works once the uncommercialised assets are removed from it: Return on Capital Employed of 11.80% in FY25 (14.03% FY24, 5.31% FY23) against an 'Adjusted ROCE' of 27.71% in FY25 (24.59% FY24) which the DRHP states is computed after excluding the capital employed and profit or loss attributable to Knovea Pharmaceutical Private Limited and Symbiotec Zenfold Private Limited — the two Subsidiaries that hold precisely the plants not yet commercialised. The distance between 11.80% and 27.71% is the size of the bet.

Operating cash collapsed in the year of peak spending: net cash flow from operating activities fell from ₹1,875.02 million (FY24) to ₹472.56 million (FY25), a CFO-to-EBITDA ratio of 0.23 times against 1.06 times a year earlier, driven by a ₹(1,314.83) million movement in trade and other payables — against capital expenditure of ₹3,081.21 million in the same restated cash flow statement.

Leverage more than doubled and liquidity turned negative: total borrowings ₹2,178.78 million (FY23) to ₹2,472.07 million (FY24) to ₹5,409.23 million (FY25) and ₹5,191.24 million at June 30, 2025; total current liabilities of ₹4,681.41 million exceeded total current assets of ₹4,594.56 million, a current ratio of 0.97 against 1.04, 1.45 and 1.75 at the three preceding balance-sheet dates.

Work in progress now exceeds the working plant, and part of it has slipped: capital work-in-progress was ₹6,326.46 million at June 30, 2025 against net property, plant and equipment of ₹3,957.50 million, and the DRHP's own overdue-CWIP ageing table shows ₹2,737.11 million of projects overdue against their original schedule at June 30, 2025, up from ₹2,427.22 million at March 31, 2025 and ₹1,251.88 million at March 31, 2024, against nil at March 31, 2023.

Fiscal 2025 profit fell while EBITDA rose: profit for the year declined 3.27% to ₹967.85 million from ₹1,000.55 million, even though EBITDA rose to ₹2,061.12 million from ₹1,770.41 million. The DRHP prints the causes — total tax expense up 62.28% from ₹309.28 million to ₹501.90 million, and finance costs from ₹72.36 million to ₹160.36 million. The stated FY23-to-FY25 PAT CAGR of 103.00% rests on a depressed FY23 base of ₹234.86 million.

Reported revenue growth of 4.93% in FY25 is flattered by a base effect the DRHP itself footnotes: revenue from operations for Fiscal 2024 includes milestone revenue of ₹442.11 million with a corresponding nil in Fiscal 2025, and after excluding it the printed growth figures become 11.83% for Fiscal 2025 and 18.63% for Fiscal 2024. The higher of the two published growth rates is the one on the denominator that carries the milestone.

The Offer is 93% secondary and buys the Company no new capacity: an Offer for Sale of up to ₹20,300.00 million (Rosewood Investments ₹12,500.00 million, India Business Excellence Fund - III ₹6,000.00 million, Satwani Holdings LLP ₹1,800.00 million) against a Fresh Issue of up to ₹1,500.00 million, of which ₹1,125.00 million goes to prepayment or repayment of two cash-credit facilities and the remainder to general corporate purposes printed as '[●]' — no capital-expenditure object at all, immediately after a ₹7,405.16 million build-out.

13.22% of pre-Offer capital is pledged inside the syndicate: 8,298,243 Equity Shares held by the Promoters and three Promoter Group family trusts are pledged to Beacon Trusteeship Limited under an unattested pledge agreement dated December 10, 2025 as amended December 18, 2025, securing debentures of Satwani Holdings (India) Private Limited held by Nomura Capital (India) Private Limited — an affiliate of BRLM Nomura Financial Advisory and Securities (India) Private Limited. Separately, BRLM Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors Limited is confined to marketing the Offer because Investor Selling Shareholder India Business Excellence Fund - III is its associate.

Revenue rests on a handful of molecules sold to a handful of buyers with nothing contractual behind it: top five products were 66.36%, 60.37%, 63.16% and 65.11% of revenue from operations across FY23, FY24, FY25 and Q1FY26 and top ten 81.49% to 83.15%; top ten customers were 60.65%, 61.65%, 55.90% and 64.01% of revenue from sale of products. The DRHP states 'we do not maintain long-term contractual arrangements with our customers and rely on purchase orders', and the same is true upstream — raw materials are procured on purchase orders with no long-term supplier agreements.

Working capital is inventory-heavy and lengthening on the receivable side: inventory turnover days of 260.39 (FY24), 282.89 (FY25) and 202.38 (Q1FY26), with trade receivable days rising 61 to 73 to 78; the DRHP prints no payable days and no cash-conversion-cycle figure at all, so the cycle cannot be read whole from the document.

Statutory auditor modifications ran in both of the last two audited years: a CARO clause (i)(c) qualification for Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024 on title deeds of one leasehold immovable property of ₹375.24 million carrying value not held in the Company's name (attributed to Subsidiaries Symbiotec Zenfold ₹157.29 million and Knovea Pharmaceutical ₹217.95 million, each standing in the name of STI India Limited), and an audit-trail qualification for both years — the edit log was not enabled for changes made through privileged or administrative access, and the table-level logging parameter remained inactive until April 26, 2024.

Company-law hygiene has two open items dating back a decade or more: no whole-time company secretary was appointed for the period March 30, 2005 to January 29, 2014 despite paid-up capital crossing ₹20.00 million (Section 383A of the Companies Act, 1956), with a compounding application dated December 9, 2025 pending before the NCLT, Indore and no penalty quantified; and 11 corporate records are untraceable, spanning seven allotments between 2007 and 2013, the challans for a 2009 rights issue and a 2013 preferential allotment, a 2010 share transfer form, and the Form 32 and Form 25C for the Managing Director's own 2005 appointment.

The US FDA record is better read from the footnote than the headline: the Company states it received no critical observations from global regulators over the last three Fiscals and Q1FY26, but also that Form 483 letters were issued following both US FDA inspections — Rau in 2019 and Pithampur in 2023 — and that Rau, one of the two revenue-earning plants, has not been inspected by the US FDA in approximately six years.

Utilisation at the older plant is weak and measured against a softer denominator: Rau chemical-synthesis utilisation was 39.99% (FY23), 53.32% (FY24), 49.80% (FY25) and 70.17% (Q1FY26), and the DRHP states utilisation is computed as actual production divided by Effective Capacity, not by Maximum Capacity — effective capacity at Rau was 74.58, 68.00, 74.64 and 60.22 MT against a maximum of 96.00 MT falling to 92.00 MT.

Promoter entry costs are separated by a factor of sixteen, and the top end was created six days before filing: average cost of acquisition is ₹16.51 for Satwani Holdings LLP, ₹72.37 for Sushil Satwani, ₹273.04 for Kashish Satwani and ₹273.50 for Anil Satwani, the last two set by a rights issue of 6,999,516 Equity Shares at ₹276.00 per share completed December 13, 2025 — followed by gift transfers of 4,748,208 Equity Shares to three family trusts on December 16, 2025. Weighted average cost of acquisition of all shares transacted over one year, 18 months and three years is ₹159.69 in each period, with the acquisition-price range printed as ₹0 to ₹276.00.

Intra-group exposure is large relative to the parent's own borrowings, and the DRHP prints no total for it: loans to Knovea Pharmaceutical Private Limited of ₹2,143.08 million with a corporate guarantee of ₹1,322.00 million, to Symbiotec Zenfold Private Limited of ₹2,967.88 million with a corporate guarantee of ₹1,350.00 million, and to Navisci Pte. Ltd. of ₹117.66 million, all as of June 30, 2025 — extended to the same two Subsidiaries whose capital employed the Adjusted ROCE excludes.

The document contradicts itself on the very table used to evidence the China de-risking: the Our Business chapter prints FY25 China sourcing at 10.82%, FY23 at 12.67% and FY24 domestic sourcing at ₹758.62 million, while the identical table in MD&A and Risk Factors prints 16.82%, 34.00% and ₹785.62 million. Similar unreconciled pairs appear elsewhere — 'over 60' products against 'more than 50 products' in a capacity-table footnote, a customer-vintage table summing to 257 customers against a stated 'over 200', and 'Our business is not seasonal in nature' in MD&A against an expected Q4 shipment concentration in Risk Factor 22.

Foreign-currency exposure is stated as unhedged, against USD payables of ₹490.89 million and USD borrowings of ₹523.48 million, on a business where revenue from external customers outside India was 52.76%, 59.97%, 55.19% and 66.67% of revenue from operations across FY23 to Q1FY26 — and where the domestic figure is expressly stated to include indirect exports to regulated markets that the DRHP does not quantify.

The governance architecture is brand new and one seat has already turned over inside the filing window: all board committees were constituted by Board resolution dated November 27, 2025 and re-constituted on December 16, 2025; Independent Director Brijmohan Maheshwari was appointed November 27, 2025 and ceased December 16, 2025, a tenure of 19 days; three Nominee Directors resigned across December 2023, September 2024 and November 2025; and the DRHP discloses no board or committee meeting counts or attendance records.

Workforce attrition ran at 24.16% in FY24 (357 exits on 1,509 permanent employees) and 20.77% in FY25 (329 exits on 1,659), with FY23 printed 'N.A.' because Fiscal 2022 data is not disclosed; alongside 1,752 permanent employees at June 30, 2025 the Company engaged 490 contractual labourers — on operations the DRHP itself describes as labour-intensive.

open_questions: The ₹7,405.16 million figure appears twice in different senses — Risk Factor 21 calls it 'our capital employed' of which 53.29% is not fully commercialised, while the Business and Industry chapters call the same number the amount 'invested' in additional API and injectables capacity over the last three Fiscals and Q1FY26, and the RoCE reconciliation prints Total Capital Employed of ₹13,896.16 million at June 30, 2025. Which measure does the 53.29% attach to, and what is the not-yet-commercialised share of the ₹13,896.16 million?

What revenue, if any, has the Mhow complex-injectables facility generated since June 30, 2025, and which regulatory approvals for it have actually been granted rather than applied for? The ₹3,370.34 million was spent, capacity is 20 million vials a year, and every period in the DRHP prints nil.

CDMO revenue was ₹68.00 million in FY25 and nil in Q1FY26. What explains the gap, and what quantum has been invoiced under the three take-or-pay contracts (five-year insulin DS, ten-year classical fermentation APIs, ten-year alternate protein) whose values are nowhere printed?

How much of the ₹2,737.11 million of overdue capital work-in-progress at June 30, 2025 relates to Mhow, Ujjain and the Biologics Facility respectively, what caused the slippage, and what are the revised commissioning dates?

The ₹(1,314.83) million trade-payables movement in FY25 took payables from ₹2,276.08 million to ₹884.96 million. Was this a change in supplier credit terms, a one-off settlement, or the unwinding of an FY24 build-up — and what is the run-rate payable position now?

The Company has extended loans of ₹2,143.08 million and ₹2,967.88 million plus corporate guarantees of ₹1,322.00 million and ₹1,350.00 million to Knovea and Symbiotec Zenfold. What are the repayment terms and interest rates, and on what basis are these recoverable given both Subsidiaries are the ones excluded from Adjusted ROCE as not fully commercialised?

The Rau Facility has not been inspected by the US FDA since 2019. What were the Form 483 observations at Rau in 2019 and at Pithampur in 2023, how many were there, and have all been formally closed out?

Two printed versions of the same raw-material sourcing table disagree on China's FY25 share (16.82% versus 10.82%) and FY23 share (34.00% versus 12.67%). Which is correct, and does the correction change the stated pace of China de-risking?

The rights issue at ₹276.00 on December 13, 2025 and the gift of 4,748,208 shares to three family trusts on December 16, 2025 both fall inside the week before filing. What was the purpose of each, and how does the ₹276.00 primary issuance price relate to the Price Band still to be set?

The pledge of 13.22% of pre-Offer capital secures debentures of Satwani Holdings (India) Private Limited — a Promoter-side entity — held by an affiliate of one of the BRLMs. What is the quantum and tenor of those debentures, and what happens to the pledge if the Offer is not consummated within six months of the DRHP filing?

Independent Director Brijmohan Maheshwari was appointed on November 27, 2025 and ceased on December 16, 2025. What were the circumstances of a 19-day tenure ending three days before the DRHP was filed?

What is the expected commissioning date and capital cost of the Biologics Facility (two 7 KL reactors) at Ujjain, and how is it to be funded given the Fresh Issue carries no capital-expenditure object?

Rau chemical-synthesis utilisation was 49.80% in FY25 on effective capacity of 74.64 MT against maximum capacity of 96.00 MT, and maximum capacity then fell to 92.00 MT at Q1FY26. What drove the reduction in maximum capacity, and what is the plan for the idle Rau capacity?

verdict.our_read: An Indore corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone API maker (FY25 revenue from operations ₹7,515.54 million, PAT ₹967.85 million, stated 36.2% global corticosteroid-API volume share for Fiscal 2025 per the commissioned F&S Report) that has already spent the money on its next three businesses and has not yet earned from any of them — 53.32% of a ₹13,195.00 million Gross Block is stated as not yet fully commercialised, the ₹3,370.34 million Mhow complex-injectables facility prints nil revenue in every period shown, and 93% of the ₹21,800.00 million draft offer is a secondary sale that brings the Company nothing. strengths_observed: Franchise position is narrow but stated as dominant within it: global volume market share of 36.2% in corticosteroid APIs and 44.2% in steroidal-hormone APIs in Fiscal 2025, with molecule-level Fiscal 2025 volume shares of Hydrocortisone 78.9%, Testosterone 70.4%, Methylprednisolone 50.6%, Betamethasone 39.2% and Dexamethasone 23.8% — every one of these figures is attributed by the DRHP to the F&S Report, which the Company itself commissioned and paid for, not to audited disclosure.

Regulatory estate is deep and long-held: 65 API DMFs/CEPs at Q1FY26 (64 in each of FY25, FY24 and FY23), of which 42 DMFs registered with the US FDA and 23 CEPs from the EDQM as of June 30, 2025; US FDA approval held 16 years at Rau and 13 years at Pithampur, EU-GMP 18 and 12 years, WHO-GMP 21 and 14 years; 10 regulatory-agency inspections and over 106 customer audits completed across FY23 to Q1FY26.

Margin has stepped up hard on the existing API base: EBITDA ₹742.50 million (FY23) to ₹1,770.41 million (FY24) to ₹2,061.12 million (FY25) at margins of 12.96%, 24.48% and 27.26%, and 29.45% on ₹606.07 million in Q1FY26; Pithampur, the larger plant, ran at 89.38% chemical-synthesis and 82.52% fermentation utilisation in FY25.

The claims side of the balance sheet is effectively empty: 'There are no contingent liabilities or commitments in relation to us as at June 30, 2025 as per Ind AS 37'; every 'aggregate amount involved' cell in both litigation summary tables is printed 'Nil'; only three matters are disclosed in total (an FIR the Company itself filed in 2017, a writ petition a Subsidiary filed in 2023, and a criminal complaint against a Nominee Director concerning an unrelated company); the Company states it has no group companies; and Annexure VII Part A records no audit qualification for any of the four periods requiring corrective restatement adjustment.

China dependence has been cut, and the reduction is quantified in the DRHP's own table: raw-material imports from China fell from ₹3,119.82 million / 52.79% of total expenses in FY24 to ₹1,024.32 million in FY25 and ₹189.37 million / 11.76% in Q1FY26, alongside in-house sourcing flexibility for key starting materials covering over 80% of the product portfolio by revenue through fermentation-based backward integration.

Customer base is old rather than merely large: over 200 customers across more than 40 countries as of June 30, 2025 (over 50 domestic, over 150 export), average relationship tenure of more than ten years for the top five and more than nine years for the top ten, with 96, 89 and 68 new distinct customers added in FY25, FY24 and FY23; bad debts were nil in FY25 and Q1FY26 against ₹0.82 million (0.07%) in FY24.

The next-leg capacity is built and paid for rather than promised: as of the DRHP date the Company states aggregate maximum chemical synthesis capacity of 584.67 MT, fermentation capacity of 700 KL (up from 300 KL on the Ujjain commissioning) and complex injectables capacity of 20 million double chamber vials per annum, funded by over ₹7,405.16 million invested over the last three Fiscals and Q1FY26 — the Fresh Issue asks for no capex money.

Four named CDMO arrangements are disclosed, three of them take-or-pay: insulin drug substance for five years, classical fermentation-based APIs for ten years, and a ten-year non-pharmaceutical alternate-protein contract with a United States company, plus a GLP-1 manufacturing and supply agreement with validation batches underway. No contract value, volume or committed rupee amount is printed for any of the four.

Reported cost of the API franchise is falling relative to sales in the periods shown: cost of raw materials, packing material and consumables was 57.80%, 52.90%, 46.89% and 45.12% of total expenses across FY23, FY24, FY25 and Q1FY26, while R&D spend was ₹181.50, ₹205.09, ₹311.43 and ₹60.73 million (3.20%, 2.86%, 4.14% and 2.99% of revenue from operations) on a 138-strong R&D team including 96 master's degrees and 11 PhDs.
